contract: conformers(molecular_graph_smiles, stereochemistry, budget) -> K x N x 3 coordinates in Angstrom, N is RDKit AddHs atom order and 1<=K<=budget. Return bounded physically plausible conformers preserving all explicit stereocentres. Score molecular-macro GEOM heavy-atom symmetry-aware RMSD coverage at 0.5 Angstrom; matching RMSD is diagnostic. Evaluator checks bond distances, clashes and chirality against the molecular graph.

ChoderaLab Modelforge GEOM-QM9 nc_1000_v1.0 curation, CC0; 67 molecules/1000 actual conformers, publisher MD5 and full source SHA256 verified. 57 complete ensembles/958 conformers retained after source-only graph, valence and stereochemistry audit.

limitations: Independent SCIEL adaptation of a cited scientific problem; no claim to reproduce author leaderboard scores.
Candidate and evaluator run in one Python process; data access is separated by API, not an OS sandbox. Isolate evaluator data for adversarial or held-out evaluation.

Secondary published scientific curation of GEOM-QM9, zero-shot pilot over57 molecules/958 released conformers. No claim to cover the complete original ensemble archive, GEOM-Drugs, or experimental conformer populations.

Ten entire source ensembles excluded by graph/valence/stereochemistry checks before candidate evaluation. Source atomic order is recovered using geometry-based bond perception and verified chirality-preserving graph isomorphism; all retained reference frames pass the physical contract.
No fitted training split is used. Coverage measures the released subset only; author-curation selection may differ from the full GEOM population.

science_relevance.definition: A task is important to science when it addresses a substantive scientific or real-world problem, and a cited research paper's main objective is to solve that problem or advance understanding of it. The evidence must explain why the problem matters and how the local task represents it. Using a task to evaluate an agent, framework, or general-purpose model, or citing only a benchmark, dataset, or tool, does not establish scientific importance.
